title: Nobody in Their Own Place

concept.title: A permutation search with a rule for every position
body: Fill positions `0 .. n-1` with the numbers `0 .. n-1`, each number used once, as in a normal permutation search. The new rule is on **every single choice**: the number placed at position `p` must not be `p` itself. A choice that breaks the rule is simply not tried.

Checking a rule **while building** (instead of building everything and filtering at the end) is what makes backtracking faster than brute force: for `n = 9` there are 362880 permutations, but the search never even starts most of the arrangements that break the rule early. The answers 1, 0, 1, 2, 9, 44, 265, 1854, 14833, 133496 are known as *derangement numbers*.

statement: Count the permutations of the numbers `1, 2, ..., n` in which no number stands at its own position, that is, the number at position `i` is never `i`.
outputFormat: Print the number of such permutations.

examples.note: The permutations 2 3 1 and 3 1 2 are the only ones with no fixed place.

hints: Fill the positions one by one with numbers that are not used yet.
Skip the number that equals the position you are filling.
When all positions are filled, count one permutation.

explanation: The search fills position after position with unused numbers other than the position itself. Each complete arrangement is one derangement.
solution.complexity: Time O(D(n) * n) about, space O(n).
